Hey Devops,

From March 15, 2026, new SSL certificates will be valid for 200 days — about 7
months — instead of a full year. This is an industry-wide change affecting all
Certificate Authorities. If you have an SSL certificate today, it will stay
valid until it naturally expires. Nothing changes for you right now.

For any new certificate issued after March 15, you’ll reactivate every 200
days to keep it running. We’ll remind you 30 days before it’s due, and
automation is coming this summer to handle it all for you. Look for updates
this summer–fall, andread more in our blog
https://www.ssls.com/blog/ssl-lifespans-are-getting-shorter-heres-whats-changing-and-whats-coming-to-keep-things-simple/
.

This month’s CloudConnexa newsletter highlights two updates designed to give administrators more control and clearer guidance across complex cloud environments.

First, Exact Match for Network Applications provides more precise routing and access control, letting you configure policies for a specific domain without automatically including its subdomains.

Next, for teams navigating distributed cloud environments, our complimentary Gartner® report helps you make smarter security decisions, aligning controls with your operating model and risk appetite.

We’re also featuring an upcoming webinar with iVALT on human-verified Zero Trust access and how passwordless biometrics can help defend against credential-based and AI-driven threats.

New: Exact Match for Network Applications in CloudConnexa

We’ve introduced Exact Match for Network Applications, giving administrators more precise control over how domains are routed and accessed in CloudConnexa.

Previously, configuring a Network Application for a domain automatically included all of its subdomains. With Exact Match, you can now define a Network Application for a specific domain only — without automatically applying the same routing or access rules to its subdomains. This makes it easier to handle cases where subdomains require different policies or routing behavior.

The result is more flexible configuration, more granular access control, and better alignment with real-world application architectures. For example, you can configure one access policy for example[.]com while enforcing different routing or access controls for subdomains such as admin.example[.]com that host internal applications.

Hi team,

For the affected user that reporting intermittent connectivity towards the target server while connected to CloudConnexa, lets capture MTR test during the issue.

For the purpose of these steps “OpenVPN client” refers to the client experiencing a slow connection to resources in your network and “connector” refers to the connector that those resources are behind.

MTR test from the OpenVPN client to the resource over CloudConnexa
MTR test from the OpenVPN client to our CloudConnexa gateway IP address that the client is connected to. This MTR will show the path over the public internet from you to the Connexa server the OpenVPN client is connected to
MTR test from the connector to our CloudConnexa gateway IP address that the connector is connected to. This MTR will show the path over the public internet from you to the Connexa server the OpenVPN client is connected to

HOW TO USE MTR

First find the CloudConnexa Server OpenVPN Client/Connector is connected to :

Procedure to find the CloudConnexa Server OpenVPN Client/Connector is connected to

On Linux, just execute mtr -b -r -c 200 <IP address>



On Windows install first WinMTR from this URL link : https://sourceforge.net/projects/winmtr, then run the graphic tool as below, entering the IP address and clicking on Start. Keep it running for a couple of minutes to guarantee test accuracy.



On MacOS you will need to follow the steps here to install https://macappstore.org/mtr/. After that, you can run
mtr -b -r -c 200 <IP address>

Affected user OpenVPN Connect App logs.

CloudConnexa now supports passwordless authentication

This month’s CloudConnexa updates focus on one of the most important shifts in modern security: moving beyond passwords.

As identity-based attacks continue to dominate the threat landscape, organizations are rethinking how users authenticate—and how Zero Trust principles show up in day-to-day access decisions. With new passwordless capabilities now available in CloudConnexa, we’re making it easier to strengthen identity assurance, reduce risk, and improve the user experience without adding complexity.

You’ll also find fresh insights on the OpenVPN blog and highlights from the broader security landscape.

Go Passwordless with CloudConnexa

Passwordless Authentication for CloudConnexa (https://em.openvpn.net/e3t/Ctc/UD+113/d55Jmx04/VWXZPf2hzVtFW7yN4Z46VDs0RW8rPchQ5JCNZVN412xbY3prCCW95jsWP6lZ3mBW7p7HFG5N83cfN7hqhmz4HKy7W58nHZK3DQ-WBW8JZDcd4mmmtSW3cK-TB6YTL6HW8gSSRj98ZHWrVT0Qsj5QTqX7N1Bvgsvzxhq5N3N6225M0sJ3W15MWsY4hwp_xW8s2zx27dby6TW4nLDP_4VMt_nW5sSMTD7119l6W2w4ZhL1N4n1xW2nrqJr1Y1GryW21Q1pX2tP9L_W4ctLRS1s7SMjW45qvsn944hc_W3-1Cfj62VNBkW4fcTF72P1FlyW4sJDHy19C97yW1WjTCt31h4nCW6rbJVB79-7bsN4QPcsWGGttpN9l8N9KsyczgW522HBb7M6WfTW3Jmshv5w0FMgW2_wH1J8z67mpW5XWQ0V6kw5vcW35M64v5brht9f7WMJsx04 )

We’re excited to announce that CloudConnexa now supports passkeys, a FIDO-compliant, phishing-resistant authentication method that replaces passwords with a faster, more secure login experience.

With passkeys, you can go passwordless across CloudConnexa — not only when logging into the Admin or User Portals, but also when connecting to your WPC. When your WPC is configured for local authentication, users can authenticate with their biometrics or device PIN instead of creating, remembering, or managing passwords.

Behind the scenes, passkeys use public-key cryptography to verify identity without ever transmitting a shared secret. Your device securely stores a private key and signs a one-time challenge, which CloudConnexa verifies using the corresponding public key. The result: strong authentication that’s resistant to phishing and credential theft by design.

This capability further strengthens CloudConnexa’s Zero Trust architecture by eliminating some of the most common identity-based attack vectors in traditional VPN deployments — including phishing, credential stuffing, MFA fatigue, and man-in-the-middle attacks. With phishing-resistant authentication built in, organizations can reduce their attack surface, improve identity assurance, and align with the latest Zero Trust guidance from NIST and CISA.

Best of all, CloudConnexa includes passwordless authentication out of the box. You don’t need to deploy or integrate a third-party Identity Provider just to start using passkeys.

description:

Re: AWS SSO Access Fails in Chromium Browsers When Connected to OpenVPN
tanish.j@hiverhq.com
Hi Nino,

Thank you for the summary.

As discussed, we removed the antivirus and browser extensions that might
have been blocking Chrome access to our AWS console and Hiver internal
applications. While the workaround you suggested—whitelisting the
applications on OpenVPN—is currently working, I still have concerns
regarding the root cause.

When the VPN is disconnected, everything works perfectly. This confirms
that the behavior is specific to the VPN connection. Specifically, the
issue was caused by OpenVPN/ZTNA blocking cross-origin requests from
mail.google.com to Hiver domains, leading to CORS errors (403 /
ERR_FAILED). This prevented the Hiver Chrome extension and Analytics God
Mode from loading for multiple users.

We have now explicitly whitelisted new-analytics.hiverhq.com, which
resolved the immediate issue for the extension and Analytics God Mode.
However, whitelisting individual domains is not a sustainable long-term
solution without a proper root cause identification. We have no guarantee
that this issue will not arise again in the future.

I would like to escalate this issue on high priority for a more in-depth
debugging process. Please let us know the next steps to identify a
permanent fix and understand why OpenVPN is interfering with these
cross-origin requests.

Best regards,

Tanish Jain

Key timelines:

Starting January 15, 2026, Amazon RDS will begin disabling the creation of new RDS SQL Server 2016 database instances.
Between July 14, 2026 and September 7, 2026, any remaining instances that have not upgraded will be upgraded to SQL Server 2019 (latest minor version available) in the specified maintenance window.
Starting September 8, 2026, any remaining instances on SQL Server 2016 will be upgraded to SQL Server 2019 (latest minor version available) regardless of instances’ scheduled maintenance window.

You can restore a SQL Server 2016 database backup to any major version supported on Amazon RDS SQL Server. For more information on restoring a database in RDS see here [3].

If you have any questions, contact AWS Support through AWS Premium Support [4] or via the RDS community forum [5].

AWS Health Event

AWS Marketplace Seller Reporting now provides collections visibility

View details in service console

Hello,

We're pleased to announce that starting January 6, 2026, you'll have access to collections status information within AWS Marketplace seller reporting insights dashboard and data feeds. This information is now available in the Billed Revenue Dashboard and Billed Event Data Feed.

What's new

Collection metadata information is now included in the following seller insights reporting solutions:

Billed Revenue Dashboard

Three new fields provide visibility into payment collection status:

collected_net_revenue - The total amount AWS has successfully collected from the buyer for this transaction
uncollected_net_revenue - The total amount AWS hasn't yet collected from the buyer for this transaction
last_collection_date - The most recent date and time when AWS collected any payment from the buyer for this transaction

Billing Event Data Feed

Two enhancements give you better tracking of collection events:

action - The type of action for this event. Possible values are as follows:
INVOICED – The buyer was invoiced for the amount
COLLECTED (New) – AWS collected this amount from the buyer
DISBURSED – The seller was paid this amount. This can include a month of invoices, or be an on-demand disbursement
FORGIVEN – The buyer was invoiced for the amount, and AWS reverted the charge
action_date (New) - The date when the transaction event occurred. The specific date depends on the action type:
INVOICED – The invoice date
COLLECTED – The collection date
DISBURSED – The disbursement date
FORGIVEN – The date on which AWS recognized this transaction as forgiven

Why this matters

These enhancements give you up-to-date visibility into your payment collection status, helping you better manage your cash flow and reduce follow-ups with customers about payment status.

Log in to your AWS Marketplace Management Portal to access these new fields in your dashboards. These fields are available now with your existing data, including historic data.

Hello,

Some users of this account have not used AWS CloudShell for over 110 days in the us-west-2 Region. On January 16, 2026 we are scheduled to delete the CloudShell home directory and data of inactive users in the us-west-2 Region.

Important: You can see the list of affected users under the Affected Resources tab in your AWS Health Dashboard [1]. To stop this deletion, users that are listed in the Affected Resources tab need to launch CloudShell [2] in the us-west-2 Region.

AWS CloudShell offers a separate home directory per AWS Region, so the deletion of the home directory will occur only in the AWS Region that hasn’t been used for your CloudShell sessions in over 120 days. If you regularly use CloudShell in other AWS Regions, those separate home directories will not be affected.

Please note that this notification will persist until January 16, 2026, even if the aforementioned steps are completed.

For more information on persistent storage in AWS CloudShell, see Persistent Storage [3]. If you have any questions or concerns, please contact AWS Premium Support [4].

Hello,

AWS Lambda has detected that one or more Lambda functions in your AWS Account: 856707897744 are being invoked in a recursive loop with other AWS resources. To prevent unexpected charges from being billed to your AWS account, Lambda has stopped the recursive invocations listed in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

What do I need to do?

Please review your functions and their trigger configurations to identify any unintentional recursive patterns. To prevent further recursive invocations of your function, follow the instructions in the AWS Lambda Developer Guide [1].

If your design intentionally uses recursive patterns, you can use the recursive loop detection API to turn off recursive loop detection for the affected Lambda function(s) [2].

How do I find out when terminated invokes occurred?

Terminated invokes are tracked via the RecursiveInvocationsDropped metric. To view this metric, follow the instructions for viewing metrics on the CloudWatch console [3] and choose the metric RecursiveInvocationsDropped.

If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to AWS Support [4].

[Action Required] Amazon EKS Kubernetes 1.32 end of standard support [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]

Hello,

[AWS Health may periodically trigger reminder notifications about this communication if resources remain unresolved.]

Standard support for Kubernetes version 1.32 in Amazon EKS will end on March 23, 2026. Starting this date Amazon EKS clusters running on 1.32 with Kubernetes version policy set to extended will enter extended support. Kubernetes version 1.32 will remain in extended support until March 23, 2027. After March 23, 2027, Kubernetes 1.32 will no longer be supported on Amazon EKS, and all Amazon EKS clusters running on 1.32 will be automatically updated to Kubernetes version 1.33.

You are receiving this message because you currently have 1 or more Amazon EKS clusters running on Kubernetes version 1.32. If you have deleted, or already upgraded your EKS cluster, please disregard this message.

A list of your affected resource(s) can be found in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

Amazon EKS clusters in extended support receive ongoing security patches for the Kubernetes control plane. Additionally, Amazon EKS releases critical patches for Amazon VPC CNI, kube-proxy, and CoreDNS add-ons, AWS-published EKS Optimized Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) for Amazon Linux and Bottlerocket, and EKS Fargate nodes for Kubernetes versions in extended support. All clusters in extended support are backed by technical support from AWS.

If you do not want to use extended support, we recommend that you update your 1.32 clusters to Kubernetes version 1.33 or newer before March 23, 2026. You can also opt-out of extended support by managing your Kubernetes version policy [1]. Amazon EKS clusters that are opted-out of extended support will have their control planes automatically upgraded at the end of standard support.

To learn more about the extended support versions pricing, see our announcement [2]. For instructions on how to update your cluster(s), see the Amazon EKS service documentation [3].

To learn more on Kubernetes version support, see the Amazon EKS service documentation [4].

If you have questions or concerns, please contact AWS support [5].

[Action Required] AWS Lambda recursive loop detected and auto-remediated in your account [Account ID: 856707897744]

View details in service console

Hello,

AWS Lambda has detected that one or more Lambda functions in your AWS Account: 856707897744 are being invoked in a recursive loop with other AWS resources. To prevent unexpected charges from being billed to your AWS account, Lambda has stopped the recursive invocations listed in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

What do I need to do?

Please review your functions and their trigger configurations to identify any unintentional recursive patterns. To prevent further recursive invocations of your function, follow the instructions in the AWS Lambda Developer Guide [1].

If your design intentionally uses recursive patterns, you can use the recursive loop detection API to turn off recursive loop detection for the affected Lambda function(s) [2].

How do I find out when terminated invokes occurred?

Terminated invokes are tracked via the RecursiveInvocationsDropped metric. To view this metric, follow the instructions for viewing metrics on the CloudWatch console [3] and choose the metric RecursiveInvocationsDropped.

If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to AWS Support [4].

To prevent unexpected charges from being billed to your AWS account, Lambda has stopped the recursive invocations listed in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

What do I need to do?

Please review your functions and their trigger configurations to identify any unintentional recursive patterns. To prevent further recursive invocations of your function, follow the instructions in the AWS Lambda Developer Guide [1].

If your design intentionally uses recursive patterns, you can use the recursive loop detection API to turn off recursive loop detection for the affected Lambda function(s) [2].

How do I find out when terminated invokes occurred?

Terminated invokes are tracked via the RecursiveInvocationsDropped metric. To view this metric, follow the instructions for viewing metrics on the CloudWatch console [3] and choose the metric RecursiveInvocationsDropped.

If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to AWS Support [4].

Hello,

AWS Lambda has detected that one or more Lambda functions in your AWS Account: 856707897744 are being invoked in a recursive loop with other AWS resources. To prevent unexpected charges from being billed to your AWS account, Lambda has stopped the recursive invocations listed in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

What do I need to do?

Please review your functions and their trigger configurations to identify any unintentional recursive patterns. To prevent further recursive invocations of your function, follow the instructions in the AWS Lambda Developer Guide [1].

If your design intentionally uses recursive patterns, you can use the recursive loop detection API to turn off recursive loop detection for the affected Lambda function(s) [2].

How do I find out when terminated invokes occurred?

Terminated invokes are tracked via the RecursiveInvocationsDropped metric. To view this metric, follow the instructions for viewing metrics on the CloudWatch console [3] and choose the metric RecursiveInvocationsDropped.

If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to AWS Support [4].

Standard support for Kubernetes version 1.32 in Amazon EKS will end on March 23, 2026. Starting this date Amazon EKS clusters running on 1.32 with Kubernetes version policy set to extended will enter extended support. Kubernetes version 1.32 will remain in extended support until March 23, 2027. After March 23, 2027, Kubernetes 1.32 will no longer be supported on Amazon EKS, and all Amazon EKS clusters running on 1.32 will be automatically updated to Kubernetes version 1.33.

You are receiving this message because you currently have 1 or more Amazon EKS clusters running on Kubernetes version 1.32. If you have deleted, or already upgraded your EKS cluster, please disregard this message.

A list of your affected resource(s) can be found in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

Amazon EKS clusters in extended support receive ongoing security patches for the Kubernetes control plane. Additionally, Amazon EKS releases critical patches for Amazon VPC CNI, kube-proxy, and CoreDNS add-ons, AWS-published EKS Optimized Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) for Amazon Linux and Bottlerocket, and EKS Fargate nodes for Kubernetes versions in extended support. All clusters in extended support are backed by technical support from AWS.

If you do not want to use extended support, we recommend that you update your 1.32 clusters to Kubernetes version 1.33 or newer before March 23, 2026. You can also opt-out of extended support by managing your Kubernetes version policy [1]. Amazon EKS clusters that are opted-out of extended support will have their control planes automatically upgraded at the end of standard support.

To learn more about the extended support versions pricing, see our announcement [2]. For instructions on how to update your cluster(s), see the Amazon EKS service documentation [3].

To learn more on Kubernetes version support, see the Amazon EKS service documentation [4].

If you have questions or concerns, please contact AWS support [5].

name: Your CloudConnexa December Newsletter
description:
Thu, 18 Dec 2025 10:25:25 -0800
Your CloudConnexa December Newsletter
newsletter@openvpn.com
New CloudConnexa API controls, plus our Zero Trust webinar—now on demand

This month’s CloudConnexa updates focus on giving admins more control and flexibility as Zero Trust environments continue to evolve. From new granular API key permissions that strengthen security and simplify automation to an on-demand webinar on building a modern Zero Trust strategy, these updates are designed to help you scale securely and with confidence.

In addition, Audit Log (https://em.openvpn.net/e3t/Ctc/UD+113/d55Jmx04/VWrvkB4JcNzwW8G11rC1pdnyjW61z83B5HcMKvMtGxm43prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3nXN8Q1ggT7HtzSW6mdj-g4l-TBKW3QdW2S3jqrSJW4SqcD73-ZbT3W205WcB9gYNKsW7zzKWH8jmj6vW4Kf7l_3QfH_7W7Dr6hR18qD6QW2zRwlK4nXf2DW6WpCg02tjRQrN7p29jnYqDZgVcHW4P4-CgrfW6Z-kdW943PMQW30VwfR2bVM1FN14gkCG1pS8yW34fKHR5GLy3MW7P4JYc8Cq_hXW8Ttmzc1tbZJ8W2vc6CP1BqH87W992CFj45sTDcN4l63S9JRlrdW3sLwdp3zcmRsW5vK1M056TVjNW4vhwzz55-x2Mf6Wwt2804 ) and DNS Log (https://em.openvpn.net/e3t/Ctc/UD+113/d55Jmx04/VWrvkB4JcNzwW8G11rC1pdnyjW61z83B5HcMKvMtGxm43prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3m1W552J6V6fp2f_W7G44SP8c2R2_W2YkCFD2TrbjKW2-FgRD5cnW4SW3Y4Nb544McxFW5KgRl95414w5W4rFlvl511l5SW19B0gb1r-SL9W1fwr4m62-LjxW61hYq46nwJkxVPK97s4Gh1JnW4hqFNG3LJLXsW8rWkbj1p0cHkVQ3JD56KmczsW5FJ_-v627q_qW88WQ-f550Nx_N7s3BfSL9f22W432tZ98WjcpKW1_VWBL1Gl4C-N68HYd0GsKbhW7cBklC39Vzj3VJYRlw8dwnyZVsQNMh8Tz_23W2X6Sdn6t27Hmf2tv3Kj04 ) have officially moved out of beta, with some small improvements that enhance accuracy, consistency, and accessibility.

And here’s a bonus teaser: The OpenVPN team has been hard at work bringing passwordless authentication to CloudConnexa. It’s another step in our commitment to advancing Zero Trust and helping organizations — especially those in highly regulated industries — meet modern security and privacy standards. Keep an eye out for a deeper dive in next month’s newsletter. In the meantime, you can explore the documentation here (https://em.openvpn.net/e3t/Ctc/UD+113/d55Jmx04/VWrvkB4JcNzwW8G11rC1pdnyjW61z83B5HcMKvMtGxlv5m_5PW69t95C6lZ3mNW93Z6Fc8W4wlZW8qfzMM63lwcsW2msqq68FrDjpVSf-zQ2TcGzXW4GHDxR7fM_4KMxyNtcmqHmfVbkSqB4wXkJvW5P5Ky95ZkqM9W5QN_mG7HQCs2W4sqgP02dlJgqW19Bvh1852-b8W7_NDDn4rrLZhVbSZWT4zlr_hW30Fdk34__nYTW1DC56b5Tg7kSN83cj6Cc4pl9VBMjg26lScQFW3Dm4lp4tQGSJW96T5KS124dx7W20RRRq69PS57W36xMTd4rpv7NW4V82QD8W0fW6W3vlC0s136lDKN7ftjHnCzttVW20xkmg361gC4W6SRZNM3q6XYwW701mL47cL_m6W48tsW-3v6RpwN3DRX6RyZFTlW5gP3vD4NMP2cW378Sbz9c778GW8gW7jz3gyCXrW7Bl6cw4PBZPqV8fW8n6WSMLDW9bkbwt1hWbfBW4jh7r496hXfwf8kVVF004 ) .

Enhance API Security & Automation with Granular API Key Controls

New API Key Controls in CloudConnexa API 1.2.0 graphic (https://em.openvpn.net/e3t/Ctc/UD+113/d55Jmx04/VWrvkB4JcNzwW8G11rC1pdnyjW61z83B5HcMKvMtGxmn3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3nrW9d9g8W74xjllW8Q4bFs8gnVkmW4chh-n5TMdVjW8JwdFP21B5GWW7yNJNW8Kjt7_N1trBV2McdTnW1DT7V47NkX_bW2CH3Dd3fmL-CW9gCx6t6jt9_MW1f0Dsd2GBjvsW1VrN9v33Mq15W2_g5KS2ygcHYN400Sjhy2LqnV59dsf37NMCxW1J7XJ_8-gfdnW4hcQlP4B2J02W6P2CNx2mTvNTW8lSX4t4nDY96W16JSMp7_2wzrW24qnLs9kWmccW5q82vr1B4mLNW12Y2MS8ThzmpW8stGlZ580nJtN2pJskVFkh5VW84W8pK23StN2W5Qzb-D5bylgvf41LL7l04 )

CloudConnexa API 1.2.0 introduces granular API key controls that give administrators more precision and security over API credentials.

Granular API Permissions

Admins can now define exactly which resources an API key can read or modify — and update permissions anytime before it expires.

This helps you:

Enforce least-privilege access aligned with Zero Trust.
Safely integrate with contractors or third-party tools.
Reduce the impact of compromised credentials.
Avoid exposing full access to Access Groups, Users, Logs, and more.
Support multi-team environments with role-specific API keys.

CloudConnexa UI (https://em.openvpn.net/e3t/Ctc/UD+113/d55Jmx04/VWrvkB4JcNzwW8G11rC1pdnyjW61z83B5HcMKvMtGxmn3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3nrW9d9g8W74xjllW8Q4bFs8gnVkmW4chh-n5TMdVjW8JwdFP21B5GWW7yNJNW8Kjt7_N1trBV2McdTnW1DT7V47NkX_bW2CH3Dd3fmL-CW9gCx6t6jt9_MW1f0Dsd2GBjvsW1VrN9v33Mq15W2_g5KS2ygcHYN400Sjhy2LqnV59dsf37NMCxW1J7XJ_8-gfdnW4hcQlP4B2J02W6P2CNx2mTvNTW8lSX4t4nDY96W16JSMp7_2wzrW24qnLs9kWmccW5q82vr1B4mLNW12Y2MS8ThzmpW8stGlZ580nJtN2pJskVFkh5VW84W8pK23StN2W5Qzb-D5bylgvf41LL7l04 )

Other API 1.2.0 Enhancements: Improved Control & Smarter API Responses

New endpoints let you activate or suspend Host and Network Connectors, improving automation and seat utilization. IPsec connector responses now include your CloudConnexa gateway’s public IP, and device queries return the installed OpenVPN Connect version for easier troubleshooting and compliance.

Get Started

Go to API & Logs > API.
Click Create Credentials.
Scroll to Permissions.
Check “Read Only” and/or “Modify” for each resource.
Click Create to create the new API key.

To learn more, see the CloudConnexa API v1.2.0 release notes below:

Check out the Release Notes

name: Important Update: Changes to your AWS Marketplace Management Portal experience
description:
Wed, 17 Dec 2025 16:32:46 +0000
Important Update: Changes to your AWS Marketplace Management Portal experience
devops@grexit.com
96

AWS Health Event

View in Notification Center

Important Update: Changes to your AWS Marketplace Management Portal experience

View details in service console

Hello,

We want to inform you about changes to the AWS Marketplace Management Portal (AMMP). These changes are being rolled out in phases between now and February 1, 2026; some partners will see these changes sooner than others.

What’s changing?

On November 30, 2025, we launched a new AWS Partner Central experience in the AWS Management Console: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/apn/announcing-aws-partner-central-in-the-aws-management-console

This new experience consolidates access to all Partner Central and AWS Marketplace Management Portal (AMMP) features. Now, partners can use a single set of credentials to manage their entire sales cycle, from deal progression to sale and transaction on the AWS Marketplace.

How does this impact me?

This new, consolidated experience includes a re-designed navigation panel that includes all Partner Central and Marketplace features. Instead of a navigation bar at the top of the AMMP portal, users will see a new navigation bar on the left-side panel that aligns with the AWS console navigation. Additionally, the registration process for a new seller account will be accessible from the new Partner Central console service page and the existing AMMP registration will be removed on February 1, 2026: https://us-east-1.console.aws.amazon.com/partnercentral/home?region=us-east-1

Existing APN Partners:

• New left-side navigation menu: Partners who are also registered AWS Marketplace Sellers will see this new navigation menu in their AMMP experience even if their organization has not yet migrated their existing Partner Central account. This does not mean your Partner Central account has been migrated; work with your alliance lead to migrate to the new experience. All partners will be required to migrate by September 30, 2026: https://partnercentral.awspartner.com/partnercentral2/s/article?category=Introductory_resources&article=Partner-Central-Migration-Guide

• Account Summary widget: Users will see a new dashboard in their AWS account associated with their AWS Marketplace activity, with an Account Summary widget. If the Partner Central account status on this dashboard appears as ‘Not Registered’, this means your organization has not yet migrated to the new Partner Central experience; work with your alliance lead to migrate to the new experience: https://partnercentral.awspartner.com/partnercentral2/s/article?category=Introductory_resources&article=Partner-Central-Migration-Guide

• Access to new features: In the new experience, Sellers who are already AWS Partners can now access Partner Central News & Events on their dashboard for a curated collection of updates, including launch announcements, key deadlines, and relevant workshops, summits or keynote events. These sellers will also have access to a new personalized chatbot with the AWS Partner Assistant extension in Amazon Q: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/partner-central/latest/getting-started/partner-assistant.html

AWS Marketplace Sellers (Non-registered APN Partners):

• New left-side navigation menu: AWS Marketplace Sellers who are not registered as a Partner in the APN will see new menu options, such as Opportunities and Leads, however they will not have access to these features until they complete the APN registration process.

• Account Summary widget: Users will see a new dashboard in their AWS account associated with their AWS Marketplace activity, with an Account Summary widget. If a Seller does not have an existing Partner Central account and is therefore not registered as an APN Partner, the Partner Central account status on this dashboard will show as ‘Not Registered’.

• Multi-product solutions: Sellers will see a new Solutions tab in the left-side navigation menu. Partners can now build solutions by combining AWS Marketplace products from both their own portfolio and other sellers' portfolios, enabling the creation of joint GTM solutions. If two or more products are attached, this composite solution can be listed and sold on the AWS Marketplace. For more information, see here: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/multi-product-solutions.html

Next steps:

• Existing partners: If your organization already has a Partner Central account, do not complete the registration process, please work with your alliance lead to migrate to the new experience. If your organization has successfully migrated to the new experience, your Partner Central account status will show as ‘Registered’ in the Account Summary widget in the console, and no action is needed: https://partnercentral.awspartner.com/partnercentral2/s/article?category=Introductory_resources&article=Partner-Central-Migration-Guide

• New partners: If you are not yet a member of the AWS Partner Network, learn more about the benefits of being in the APN [https://aws.amazon.com/partners/].

If you have any questions about these changes or need assistance with migration, contact the AWS Marketplace Seller Operations team: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/contact-us/

name: SSL Notice: Changes Affecting Client Authentication EKU
description:
Wed, 17 Dec 2025 13:01:57 +0000 (UTC)
SSL Notice: Changes Affecting Client Authentication EKU
devops@grexit.com
SSLs.com An upcoming change to Client Auth EKU. No action needed for HTTPS-only
use.

https://www.ssls.com/ View in browser
https://links.ssls.com/e/evib?_t=b24c6b7c850d49af9417e6878ae89af7&_m=14affad8c5dd4d7893b5ecaa5544397c&_e=ZILWAX_l-_vyPSHQeF3QPxBTMFmFZAevkGPRofnOvQtEk6Ew55DTg4m8fVILES_-

Dear Customer,

We’re sharing an update that affects only a small subset of SSL users,
specifically those who use certificates for Client Authentication or mTLS.
Since we can’t determine how every certificate is used, we’re notifying all
customers as a precaution.

If you use SSL certificates only for standard website security (HTTPS), no
action is required.

What’s happening

The CA/Browser Forum is requiring Certificate Authorities to remove the Client
Authentication EKU from all publicly trusted SSL/TLS certificates. Sectigo, our
upstream provider, will follow this rule and remove Client Auth EKU from all
new certificates starting May 15, 2026. Existing certificates are not affected
and remain valid until they expire.

Who is affected

Only customers who use SSL certificates for:

•

Client Authentication

•

mTLS

•

Server-to-server authentication

If your certificates are used exclusively for HTTPS, you are not affected.

What you need to do

If you rely on Client Authentication, you will no longer be able to use
publicly trusted SSL/TLS certificates for this purpose once the Client Auth EKU
is removed.

To remain compliant, you should either:

•

Move to a Private PKI solution, or

•

Update your systems to stop requiring the Client Auth EKU.

Sectigo offers Private PKI
https://www.sectigo.com/enterprise-solutions/certificate-manager/private-pki
options that fully support mTLS and Client Authentication. These must be
purchased directly from Sectigo, as they are not available through SSLs.com.

Need help?

If you have any questions or concerns, please email us at support@ssls.com
mailto:support@ssls.com or chat with us https://www.ssls.com.

You got this email because you subscribed to our emails rock. We respect your
privacy. Stay savvy. © SSLs.com, AZ 85034, USA

AWS Lambda has detected that one or more Lambda functions in your AWS Account: 856707897744 are being invoked in a recursive loop with other AWS resources. To prevent unexpected charges from being billed to your AWS account, Lambda has stopped the recursive invocations listed in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

What do I need to do?

Please review your functions and their trigger configurations to identify any unintentional recursive patterns. To prevent further recursive invocations of your function, follow the instructions in the AWS Lambda Developer Guide [1].

If your design intentionally uses recursive patterns, you can use the recursive loop detection API to turn off recursive loop detection for the affected Lambda function(s) [2].

How do I find out when terminated invokes occurred?

Terminated invokes are tracked via the RecursiveInvocationsDropped metric. To view this metric, follow the instructions for viewing metrics on the CloudWatch console [3] and choose the metric RecursiveInvocationsDropped.

Hello,

[AWS Health may periodically trigger reminder notifications about this communication if resources remain unresolved.]

We are contacting you as we have identified that your AWS Account currently has one or more AWS Lambda functions using the Python 3.9 runtime.

We are ending support for Python 3.9 in Lambda on December 15, 2025. This follows Python 3.9 End-Of-Life (EOL) reached on October 30, 2025 [1]. End of support does not impact function execution. Your functions will continue to run. However, they will be running on an unsupported runtime which is no longer maintained or patched by the AWS Lambda team.

As described in the Lambda runtime support policy [2], end of support for language runtimes in Lambda happens in several stages.

Starting on December 15, 2025, Lambda will no longer apply security patches and other updates to the Python 3.9 runtime used by Lambda functions, and functions using Python 3.9 will no longer be eligible for technical support. Also, Python 3.9 will no longer be available in the AWS Console, although you can still create and update functions using Python 3.9 via AWS CloudFormation, the AWS CLI, AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM), or other tools.
Starting June 1, 2026, you will no longer be able to create new Lambda functions using the Python 3.9 runtime.
Starting July 1, 2026, you will no longer be able to update existing functions using the Python 3.9 runtime.

We recommend that you upgrade your existing Python 3.9 functions to the latest available Python runtime in Lambda before December 15, 2025.

Your impacted Lambda functions using the Python 3.9 runtime are listed on the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

This notification is generated for functions using the Python 3.9 runtime for the $LATEST function version. The following command shows how to use the AWS CLI [3] to list all functions in a specific region that is using Python 3.9, including published function versions. To find all such functions in your account, repeat the following command for each region:

aws lambda list-functions --region us-east-1 --output text --query "Functions[?Runtime=='python3.9'].FunctionArn"

Starting 180 days before deprecation, you can also use Trusted Advisor to identify functions using the Python 3.9 runtime [4].

If you have any concerns or require further assistance, please contact AWS Support [5].

[Action Required] Amazon EKS Kubernetes 1.32 end of standard support [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]

View details in service console

Hello,

[AWS Health may periodically trigger reminder notifications about this communication if resources remain unresolved.]

Standard support for Kubernetes version 1.32 in Amazon EKS will end on March 23, 2026. Starting this date Amazon EKS clusters running on 1.32 with Kubernetes version policy set to extended will enter extended support. Kubernetes version 1.32 will remain in extended support until March 23, 2027. After March 23, 2027, Kubernetes 1.32 will no longer be supported on Amazon EKS, and all Amazon EKS clusters running on 1.32 will be automatically updated to Kubernetes version 1.33.

You are receiving this message because you currently have 1 or more Amazon EKS clusters running on Kubernetes version 1.32. If you have deleted, or already upgraded your EKS cluster, please disregard this message.

A list of your affected resource(s) can be found in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

Amazon EKS clusters in extended support receive ongoing security patches for the Kubernetes control plane. Additionally, Amazon EKS releases critical patches for Amazon VPC CNI, kube-proxy, and CoreDNS add-ons, AWS-published EKS Optimized Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) for Amazon Linux and Bottlerocket, and EKS Fargate nodes for Kubernetes versions in extended support. All clusters in extended support are backed by technical support from AWS.

If you do not want to use extended support, we recommend that you update your 1.32 clusters to Kubernetes version 1.33 or newer before March 23, 2026. You can also opt-out of extended support by managing your Kubernetes version policy [1]. Amazon EKS clusters that are opted-out of extended support will have their control planes automatically upgraded at the end of standard support.

To learn more about the extended support versions pricing, see our announcement [2]. For instructions on how to update your cluster(s), see the Amazon EKS service documentation [3].

To learn more on Kubernetes version support, see the Amazon EKS service documentation [4].

If you have questions or concerns, please contact AWS support [5].

[1] https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/disable-extended-support.html

api-oauth-dev-verification-reply+25m4rb980kmqt1d@google.com
Hello Google Developer,

Thank you for your patience. Please see our answer to your questions below:

Can our existing CASA assessment and verification be extended to
cover "Hiver Omni" under the same project and scopes?

Please note that each OAuth project must undergo its own individual
assessment. This also applies to region-based apps and white label or
single tenant apps that share the same codebase.

Are any additional steps, documentation, or configuration changes required
in the OAuth consent screen or verification process to formally include the
new product name and usage?

For that, if this is for other project then it needs to meet all of our
verification requirements before you proceed with Security assessment. Once
you submit your new project for review, we'll review it just like how we
review these project.

If we reduce the scope (by removing delete functionality), does this
necessitate restarting the CASA certification process?

CASA recertification is done annually. This means, reducing the
functionality of your app will not change the annual recertification of
your project. As long as you are continously using the approved restricted
scope on your app, then you are require to renew your LoV annually.

Thank you and hope this answer your questions.
The Third Party Data Safety Team

[Action Required] Amazon RDS Performance Insights console deprecation timeline extended to June 30, 2026 [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]

View details in service console

Hello,

We are reaching out because you have Performance Insights enabled for your Amazon RDS and/or Amazon Aurora databases. We are extending the deprecation date of Performance Insights dashboard in the RDS console [1] and flexible retention period based pricing [2] from November 30, 2025, to June 30, 2026.

CloudWatch Database Insights [3] is our new comprehensive database observability solution. It offers an expanded set of capabilities over Performance Insights, such as fleet-level monitoring, application performance monitoring through CloudWatch Application Signals, and advanced root-cause analysis features like lock contention diagnostics.

Actions Required:

Review your Performance Insights usage and monitoring requirements. Choose CloudWatch Database Insights mode (Standard or Advanced) [3] based on your needs. See the user documentation [4] for details on the two modes and the pricing page [5] for information on its pricing.
Update infrastructure as code tools (CloudFormation, Terraform) to use Database Insights [6]
Important: Taking no action defaults all instances to Standard (free) mode on July 1, 2026, losing performance history beyond 7 days and all advanced features.

As a reminder, these are the changes that will take place on June 30, 2026:

The Performance Insights dashboard in the RDS console will be deprecated and all the links to the dashboard will be redirected to the CloudWatch Database Insights dashboard.
Performance Insights flexible retention periods (1 to 24 months) along with their pricing will be deprecated. If your current Performance Insights retention period is between 16 and 24 months, please note that the Advanced mode of CloudWatch Database Insights has a retention limit of up to 15 months. When you upgrade to CloudWatch Database Insights, you will not be able to access performance data older than 15 months.
The Execution Plan Capture feature [7] for RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server (currently available in the Performance Insights free tier) will transition to the Advanced mode of CloudWatch Database Insights.

Note: You can continue using Performance Insights APIs after June 30, 2026, as there are no changes to their functionality. However, all charges associated with their usage will now be visible under charges for CloudWatch on your AWS bill.

Credits Program: We continue to offer a credits program if you upgrade to Database Insights Advanced mode before November 30, 2025. The credits will cover the incremental cost difference between Performance Insights and Database Insights between June 1, 2025, and December 31, 2025, (inclusive). Your RDS and Aurora instances are eligible if they had Performance Insights paid-tier enabled prior to May 30, 2025, and the upgrade to CloudWatch Database Insights Advanced mode happens prior to November 30, 2025. RDS for Oracle/SQL Server with Performance Insights free-tier enabled prior to May 30, 2025, are also eligible for credits if they are upgraded to CloudWatch Database Insights Advanced mode prior to November 30, 2025.

A list of your Performance Insights enabled instances that require action can be found in the "Affected resources" tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

If you have any questions or concerns, please contact AWS Support [8]

Hello,

[AWS Health may periodically trigger reminder notifications about this communication if resources remain unresolved.]

You are receiving this message because you have one or more Amazon ElastiCache for Redis OSS replication groups running version 4.x.x or 5.x.x in the US-WEST-2 Region.

Versions 4 and 5 for Redis OSS have already reached their community End of Life in 2022. Amazon ElastiCache Standard support for these versions will end on January 31, 2026. We are providing you this notice to give you sufficient time to plan your upgrade strategy. We recommend upgrading to Amazon ElastiCache version 8 for Valkey or later. Alternatively, you can upgrade to ElastiCache v6 for Redis OSS or later versions.

Our most recommended offering is Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey 8. With Serverless, you get automatic scaling and zero-downtime upgrades.

If you prefer to continue with node-based ElastiCache, you can initiate the upgrade using either the service update APIs for an automatic upgrade to ElastiCache version 8 for Valkey, or the Modify APIs to upgrade to ElastiCache v6 for Redis OSS, ElastiCache version 8 for Valkey, or later versions. The upgrade process is fully managed, and we recommend taking a snapshot of your cluster [1] before upgrading. While most applications will not require any modification, we recommend reviewing the version compatibility page [2] and testing your application with the new version before upgrading. To learn more about upgrading ElastiCache major versions, review the Upgrading Versions page [3].

A list of your Amazon ElastiCache for Redis OSS replication groups using Version 4 or 5 can be found in the "Affected resources" tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

We want to make you aware of the following milestones:

From August 1, 2025 until January 31, 2026 - You can initiate upgrades of ElastiCache version 4 and version 5 for Redis OSS instances to newer versions at any time [3].
From February 1, 2026 - Clusters not upgraded will be automatically enrolled in Extended Support with additional charges.
Extended Support Period - February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2029
After January 31, 2029 - Any remaining clusters will be automatically upgraded to the latest version of Valkey.

During the Extended Support period, your clusters will continue to receive critical CVE security updates. However, Extended Support includes premium charges that vary depending on the year. For more information about Extended Support pricing, visit the ElastiCache pricing page [4].

If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to AWS Support [5].

[Notification] Updates to Operation Type Reporting in CUR - Effective January 6, 2026 [AWS Account: 948254249255]

View details in service console

Hello,

This is to notify you that effective January 6, 2026, we will update the "operation" values of certain Amazon Bedrock usage in AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR), CUR 2.0, and Data Exports for FOCUS to provide granular operation information. At present, when you use Serverless Models by Third-Party Providers [1] on Amazon Bedrock, the operations are labeled as "Usage" in your reports. This update will replace this generic label with specific operation types such as "InvokeModelInference" and "InvokeModelStreamingInference".

This change will provide you with more granular visibility into your Bedrock usage and associated costs, enabling better cost tracking and optimization of your model usage. No action is needed from you in order to enable this added granularity.

More details on this change are as follows:

Data Exports: This change will be implemented across all CUR versions (Legacy CUR, CUR 2.0, and FOCUS) and will affect all export formats including CSV and Parquet. The line_item_operation column in legacy CUR/CUR 2.0 and x_Operation column for FOCUS reports will reflect the granular operation types instead of the current value “Usage”. Note: this change does not affect operation data for models where we already report granular operation types.

Monthly CUR Data Transition: For all versions and formats, the January 2026 data will be handled as follows:

January 6, 2026 onwards: Data will be automatically captured with the new operation types
January 1-5, 2026 data: This data will be retroactively updated with the new operation types. This ensures that the monthly CUR data for January 2026 is complete and accurate across all formats and versions.

AWS Cost Explorer: The API Operation dimension values will also reflect these new specific operation types (such as "InvokeModelInference" and "InvokeModelStreamingInference") instead of the generic "Usage" value. This change will be visible in both the AWS Cost Explorer console and API responses.

If you have any questions or concerns regarding this upcoming change, please contact the AWS Support [2].

[1] Third-Party Providers: AI21 Labs, Anthropic, Cohere, Luma AI, Stability AI, Twelve Labs, Writer AI

[2] https://aws.amazon.com/support

Passwords Block List: Prevent common or high-risk passwords with a predefined or custom dictionary.
Password History: Ensure that users rotate passwords and restrict reuse of old passwords to reduce long-term risk.
Account Lockout: Configure login attempt limits and lockout duration to stop automated attacks.

Why it matters:

Enforce Security: Ensure strong passwords and safe practices across your organization.
Ensure Compliance: Clear visibility into enforced policies simplifies audits.
Simplify Management: Native authentication provides built-in password complexity management, eliminating reliance on external user directories or IdPs for policy enforcement.

name: [Action Required] AWS Lambda end of support for Python 3.9 [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]
description:
Fri, 14 Nov 2025 02:50:53 +0000
[Action Required] AWS Lambda end of support for Python 3.9 [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]
devops@grexit.com
96

AWS Health Event

View in Notification Center

[Action Required] AWS Lambda end of support for Python 3.9 [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]

View details in service console

Hello,

[AWS Health may periodically trigger reminder notifications about this communication if resources remain unresolved.]

We are contacting you as we have identified that your AWS Account currently has one or more AWS Lambda functions using the Python 3.9 runtime.

We are ending support for Python 3.9 in Lambda on December 15, 2025. This follows Python 3.9 End-Of-Life (EOL) reached on October 30, 2025 [1]. End of support does not impact function execution. Your functions will continue to run. However, they will be running on an unsupported runtime which is no longer maintained or patched by the AWS Lambda team.

As described in the Lambda runtime support policy [2], end of support for language runtimes in Lambda happens in several stages.

Starting on December 15, 2025, Lambda will no longer apply security patches and other updates to the Python 3.9 runtime used by Lambda functions, and functions using Python 3.9 will no longer be eligible for technical support. Also, Python 3.9 will no longer be available in the AWS Console, although you can still create and update functions using Python 3.9 via AWS CloudFormation, the AWS CLI, AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM), or other tools.
Starting February 3, 2026, you will no longer be able to create new Lambda functions using the Python 3.9 runtime.
Starting March 9, 2026, you will no longer be able to update existing functions using the Python 3.9 runtime.

We recommend that you upgrade your existing Python 3.9 functions to the latest available Python runtime in Lambda before December 15, 2025.

Your impacted Lambda functions using the Python 3.9 runtime are listed on the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

This notification is generated for functions using the Python 3.9 runtime for the $LATEST function version. The following command shows how to use the AWS CLI [3] to list all functions in a specific region that is using Python 3.9, including published function versions. To find all such functions in your account, repeat the following command for each region:

aws lambda list-functions --region us-east-1 --output text --query "Functions[?Runtime=='python3.9'].FunctionArn"

Starting 180 days before deprecation, you can also use Trusted Advisor to identify functions using the Python 3.9 runtime [4].

If you have any concerns or require further assistance, please contact AWS Support [5].

[1] https://devguide.python.org/versions/

[2] https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/runtime-support-policy.html

[3] https://aws.amazon.com/cli/

[4] https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/security-checks.html#aws-lambda-functions-deprecated-runtimes

[5] https://aws.amazon.com/support

name: [Important Update] AWS India will facilitate all AWS Marketplace transactions between Sellers and Customers in India starting November 6, 2025
description:
Thu, 6 Nov 2025 12:13:21 +0000
[Important Update] AWS India will facilitate all AWS Marketplace transactions between Sellers and Customers in India starting November 6, 2025
devops@grexit.com
96

AWS Health Event

View in Notification Center

[Important Update] AWS India will facilitate all AWS Marketplace transactions between Sellers and Customers in India starting November 6, 2025

View details in service console

Hello,

Starting November 6, 2025, AWS India (Amazon Web Services India Private Limited) will become the contracting party for business entities in India selling paid offerings to India-addressed customers on AWS Marketplace. AWS Marketplace customers based in India purchasing paid offerings from sellers in India, will receive invoices in local currency (Indian Rupee, INR).

How this affects you:

• If you are a seller organized or incorporated in India, please note the following:

o You can begin selling paid offerings through AWS Marketplace once this change has taken effect.

o You can work with an India-based Channel Partner to sell to AWS customers.

o AWS India will facilitate issuance of tax compliant invoices to AWS customers in Indian Rupees ('INR') with you as Seller of Record (SoR), as per information provided on the tax registration tab in AWS Marketplace Management Portal.

o AWS Marketplace customer invoices will include Goods and Services Tax (GST), as applicable, on all service charges.

o AWS India will collect the service charges from AWS Marketplace customers as per the generated tax compliant invoice. AWS India will remit the collected GST to you, and it is your responsibility to remit it to the tax authority.

o Disbursements from transactions with AWS customer accounts based in India will be made in INR to your registered bank account located in India.

o AWS India will do Tax Deduction at Source [referred to as Withholding Tax (WHT)] and GST- Tax Collected at Source (GST-TCS) before making your disbursements. AWS India will remit the WHT and GST-TCS to the tax authorities.

o AWS India will charge listing fee(s) with applicable GST and provide you with a tax compliant invoice.

• If you are a Channel Partner organized or incorporated in India and transact with AWS customer accounts based in India, you will receive a tax invoice for the transaction between you and your Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) who are organized or incorporated in India.

• If you are a seller organized or incorporated outside of India, please note the following:

o You can continue to sell in AWS Marketplace as-is. Invoices will continue to be issued from AWS Inc. in US Dollars (“USD”) to your customers in India.

o GST will not be charged on your listing fee(s).

• If you are a Channel Partner organized or incorporated outside of India, you can continue to sell in AWS Marketplace without making any changes. Invoices will continue to be issued from AWS Inc. in US Dollars (“USD”) to your customers in India.

The Service Terms for AWS Marketplace Sellers (“Seller Terms”) (https://aws.amazon.com/legal/seller-terms/) have been updated to reflect this change, and your continued use of AWS Marketplace after the change will constitute your acceptance of the updated Seller Terms.

Required actions:

• Actively communicate this change to your organization’s functional partners including, but not limited to, product, marketing, sales, accounting, tax, treasury, and accounts payable.

• Initiate the process of onboarding as a registered Seller on AWS Marketplace to sell your offerings to AWS customers in India. There are additional requirements for sellers to complete before they can sell to AWS customers in India via AWS India. For more details on seller onboarding requirements, tax obligations, disbursement preferences, etc., please visit our FAQ page at (https://aws.amazon.com/legal/awsin/).

If you have additional questions after reviewing the FAQs, please contact your AWS account representative or create a case with AWS Marketplace Seller Operations team (https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/contact-us/).

description:
Wed, 29 Oct 2025 08:52:50 +0000
[Action required] Validate www.hiverhq.com to renew SSL certificates
devops@grexit.com
To renew your SSL certificate, validate the domain www.hiverhq.com by updating its DNS records

Review certificate request:
https://certvalidate.cloudflare.com/validations/txt/acme?domain=www.hiverhq.com&token=JV0ebgI3J8D8MoV1SpxesRAxtHsC9PPgWxfE3IxZrKo&certificate_pack_id=c7bebbcd-e38b-41c0-a969-20b3926ed4f0

Why am I receiving this email?

In order to renew www.hiverhq.com’s SSL certificates for use on Cloudflare’s network, we need you to re-validate the domain.
If you previously validated this domain using the HTTP DCV method, there are two possible reasons why re-validation is needed:

www.hiverhq.com no longer resolves to Cloudflare's edge, and we cannot automatically complete the renewal process
Recent CA/B forum rule changes state that HTTP DCV is no longer permitted for wildcard certificates.

How do I validate www.hiverhq.com?
Add the following TXT entries to your authoritative DNS provider:

        _acme-challenge.www.hiverhq.com TXT JV0ebgI3J8D8MoV1SpxesRAxtHsC9PPgWxfE3IxZrKo

Finished adding the records above?

Complete the renewal process by clicking here: https://certvalidate.cloudflare.com/validations/txt/acme?domain=www.hiverhq.com&token=JV0ebgI3J8D8MoV1SpxesRAxtHsC9PPgWxfE3IxZrKo&certificate_pack_id=c7bebbcd-e38b-41c0-a969-20b3926ed4f0

When does my current SSL certificate expire?

The expiration date is Fri Oct 31 06:12:04 UTC 2025.

What if I can't complete validation and renew my certificate before it expires?

Please avoid letting that happen. If the SSL certificates expire, Cloudflare will remove them from the edge and your visitors may not be able to connect to www.hiverhq.com.

devops@grexit.com

Hello,

We are reaching out to you because you have enabled Performance Insights for your RDS/Aurora database instances. On November 30, 2025, we are deprecating the Performance Insights dashboard in the RDS console [1] and flexible retention periods along with their pricing [2]. Instead of Performance Insights, we recommend that you use the Advanced mode of CloudWatch Database Insights [3]. Launched on December 1, 2024, Database Insights is a comprehensive database observability solution that consolidates all database metrics, logs, and events into a unified view. It offers an expanded set of capabilities compared to Performance Insights, such as fleet-level monitoring, integration with application performance monitoring through CloudWatch Application Signals, and advanced root-cause analysis features like lock contention diagnostics [4].

These are the key changes that will take place on November 30, 2025:

The Performance Insights dashboard in the RDS console will be removed and all its links will redirect to the CloudWatch Database Insights dashboard.
The Execution Plan Capture feature [5] for RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server (currently available in the Performance Insights free tier) will transition to the Advanced mode of CloudWatch Database Insights.
The On-demand Analysis feature [6] for Aurora PostgreSQL, Aurora MySQL, and RDS for PostgreSQL (currently available in the Performance Insights paid tiers) will transition to the Advanced mode of CloudWatch Database Insights.
Performance Insights flexible retention periods (1 to 24 months) along with their pricing will be deprecated. Note that if you have selected a Performance Insights retention period between 16 and 24 months, you will lose access to performance data history beyond 15 months, even if you upgrade to the Advanced mode of Database Insights. This is because the Advanced mode of Database Insights offers a fixed retention period of 15 months for database metrics.
Performance Insights APIs will continue to exist with no pricing changes, but their costs will appear under CloudWatch alongside Database Insights charges in your AWS bill.

If you upgrade to the Advanced mode of Database Insights before November 30, 2025, we will issue credits to cover the incremental cost of your Database Insights usage from June 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025. The incremental cost is the difference between your Performance Insights charges and your Database Insights charges. Please refer to the following eligibility criteria for receiving credits.

Eligibility criteria for credit issuance:

All your RDS/Aurora instances that you upgraded from the Performance Insights paid-tier to Database Insights Advanced mode on or before May 30, 2025.
If any of your RDS/Aurora instances had the Performance Insights paid-tier enabled on any day in May 2025, and you upgrade those to the Advanced mode of Database Insights between May 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025.
All your RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server instances that you upgraded from the Performance Insights free-tier to Database Insights Advanced mode on or before May 30, 2025.
All your RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server instances for which the Performance Insights free-tier was enabled on any day in May 2025, and if you upgrade those to the Advanced mode of Database Insights between May 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025.

A list of your Performance Insights enabled instances that require action can be found in the “Affected resources” tab of your AWS Health Dashboard. Resources associated with this notification will remain in ‘pending’ status even if action required has been completed until June 10, 2025. Once resource status updates are enabled for these notifications this disclaimer will be removed.

Actions Required:

Review your current Performance Insights usage and monitoring requirements for affected instances.
Assess which mode of Database Insights [7] (Standard or Advanced) will best meet your needs. For detailed information on the features offered in each of these two modes, please refer to the user documentation [4].
If you wish to retain access to the Execution Plan Capture and On-demand Analysis features after November 30, 2025, enable the Advanced mode of Database Insights.
If you take no action, your database instances will all default to the Standard (free) mode of Database Insights after November 30, 2025. Consequently, you will lose access to performance data history beyond 7 days, as well as the execution plan and on-demand analysis features.

If you have any questions or concerns, please contact AWS Support [8].

name: [Action Required] Amazon OpenSearch Serverless Error Handling Changes [AWS Account: 948254249255]
description:
Thu, 28 Aug 2025 14:22:51 +0000
[Action Required] Amazon OpenSearch Serverless Error Handling Changes [AWS Account: 948254249255]
devops@grexit.com
[Starting September 15, 2025, emails about AWS Health events will be delivered via the AWS User Notifications service. No change is required from you to continue receiving emails. Emails about AWS Health events will be sent from a new sender address: health@aws.com and in HTML format, rather than plain text. Additionally, AWS User Notifications provides best efforts de-duplication of emails within AWS organizations and a configuration interface to manage subscriptions. Recipients may need to validate that any existing inbox rules continue to work with the changes. To switch to the new experience early, please visit https://console.aws.amazon.com/notifications/home?region=us-east-1#/managed-notifications]

Hello,

You are receiving this message because you have used Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (AOSS) and may be affected by upcoming changes to error handling. Amazon OpenSearch Serverless will be changing how it reports OCU (OpenSearch Compute Units) limit issues and internal failures on October 20, 2025.

We require you to update your application code that handles AOSS error responses before October 20, 2025, if you rely on specific error codes or messages. This change will improve clarity by providing distinct error codes for different scenarios, but may impact applications that parse or handle these responses.

Current Behavior:

Status code 507 is used for both OCU limit scenarios and internal failures
For indexing:
"status": 507,
"error": {
"type": "indexing_block_exception",
"reason": "blocked by: [maximum OCU capacity reached]"
}
For search
"status": 507,
"error": {
"type": "insufficient_storage_exception",
"reason": "current OCU capacity limit has exceeded"
}

New Behavior:

For OCU limit scenarios:
"status": 402,
"error": {
"type": "service_quota_exceeded_exception",
"reason": "maximum OCU capacity reached"
}
For internal server issues
"status": 507,
"error": {
"type": "internal_server_exception",
"reason": "Internal error occurred while processing request"
}

Recommended Changes:

If you use status code 507 to identify OCU limit scenarios, update your code to check for status code 402 instead.
If you parse error messages like "maximum OCU capacity reached" or "current OCU capacity limit has exceeded", update your parsing logic.
If you have retries configured on specific error types or reasons, update your retry logic.
Update any automated scripts or tools that make decisions based on AOSS error responses.

If you need additional time to adapt, we can temporarily disable this feature for your account. Please contact AWS Support [1] to request this accommodation.

[1] https://aws.amazon.com/support

Sincerely,
Amazon Web Services

devops@grexit.com
[Beginning September 15, 2025, emails about AWS Health events will be delivered via AWS User Notifications. AWS User Notifications provides de-duplication of emails within AWS organizations and a configuration interface to manage subscriptions. Emails about AWS Health events will be sent from a new sender address: health@aws.com and in HTML format, rather than plain text. Recipients may need to validate that email rules continue to work with the changes. To switch to the new experience early, please visit https://console.aws.amazon.com/notifications/home?region=us-east-1#/managed-notifications]

Hello,

You are receiving this message because you currently have 1 or more Amazon EKS clusters running Amazon Linux 2 (AL2) based AMIs. Amazon EKS will end support for EKS optimized AL2 AMIs on November 26, 2025.

To avoid any disruptions, please migrate your workloads to alternative AMI types before November 26, 2025. While you can continue using EKS AL2 AMIs, EKS will no longer release any new Kubernetes versions or updates to AL2 AMIs after this EOS date, including minor releases, patches, and bug fixes.

A list of your affected resource(s) can be found in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

We recommend upgrading to Amazon Linux 2023 (AL2023) or Bottlerocket AMIs. AL2023 enables a secure-by-default approach with preconfigured security policies, SELinux in permissive mode, IMDSv2-only mode enabled by default, optimized boot times, and improved package management for enhanced security and performance, well-suited for infrastructure requiring significant customizations like direct OS-level access or extensive node changes. Bottlerocket enables enhanced security, faster boot times, and a smaller attack surface for improved efficiency with its purpose-built, container-optimized design, well-suited for container-native approaches with minimal node customizations. Additionally, you can build custom EKS AL2-optimized and AL2-accelerated AMIs [1] until the EOS date (November 26, 2025), or build a custom AMI with an Amazon Linux 2 base instance until the Amazon Linux 2 EOS date (June 30, 2026).

For more information, please visit AL2023 FAQs [2], Bottlerocket FAQs [3], or refer to Amazon Linux 2 to Amazon Linux 2023 [4] or Bottlerocket AMIs [5] documentation for detailed migration guidance.

If you have questions or any challenges taking action by November 26, 2025, please see EKS AL2 & AL2-Accelerated AMIs EOS FAQs [6] or contact AWS Support [7].

Hello,

[AWS Health may periodically trigger reminder notifications about this communication if resources remain unresolved.]

Standard support for Kubernetes version 1.31 in Amazon EKS will end on November 26, 2025. Starting this date, Amazon EKS clusters running on 1.31 with Kubernetes version policy set to extended will enter extended support. Kubernetes version 1.31 will remain in extended support until November 26, 2026. After November 26, 2026, Kubernetes 1.31 will no longer be supported on Amazon EKS, and all Amazon EKS clusters running on 1.31 will be automatically updated to Kubernetes version 1.32.

You are receiving this message because you currently have 1 or more Amazon EKS clusters running on Kubernetes version 1.31. If you have deleted, or already upgraded your EKS cluster, please disregard this message.

A list of your affected resource(s) can be found in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

Amazon EKS clusters in extended support receive ongoing security patches for the Kubernetes control plane. Additionally, Amazon EKS releases critical patches for Amazon VPC CNI, kube-proxy, and CoreDNS add-ons, AWS-published EKS Optimized Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) for Amazon Linux and Bottlerocket, and EKS Fargate nodes for Kubernetes versions in extended support. All clusters in extended support are backed by technical support from AWS.

If you do not want to use extended support, we recommend that you update your 1.31 clusters to Kubernetes version 1.32 or newer before November 26, 2025. You can also opt-out of extended support by managing your Kubernetes version policy [1]. Amazon EKS clusters that are opted-out of extended support will have their control planes automatically upgraded at the end of standard support.

To learn more about the extended support versions pricing, see our announcement [2]. For instructions on how to update your cluster(s), see the Amazon EKS service documentation [3]

To learn more about Kubernetes version support, see the Amazon EKS service documentation [4]

If you have questions or concerns, please contact AWS support [5].

name: [Important Update] AWS India will soon facilitate all AWS Marketplace transactions between Sellers and Customers in India.
description:
Fri, 22 Aug 2025 20:54:13 +0000
[Important Update] AWS India will soon facilitate all AWS Marketplace transactions between Sellers and Customers in India.
devops@grexit.com
[Beginning September 15, 2025, emails about AWS Health events will be delivered via AWS User Notifications. AWS User Notifications provides de-duplication of emails within AWS organizations and a configuration interface to manage subscriptions. Emails about AWS Health events will be sent from a new sender address: health@aws.com and in HTML format, rather than plain text. Recipients may need to validate that email rules continue to work with the changes. To switch to the new experience early, please visit https://console.aws.amazon.com/notifications/home?region=us-east-1#/managed-notifications]

Hello,

AWS India (Amazon Web Services India Private Limited) will soon become the contracting party for business entities in India selling paid offerings to India-addressed customers on AWS Marketplace. AWS Marketplace customers based in India purchasing paid offerings from sellers in India will receive invoices in local currency (Indian Rupee, INR).

How this affects you:

If you are a seller organized or incorporated in India, please note the following:
• You can begin selling paid offerings through AWS Marketplace once this change has taken effect.
• You can work with an India-based Channel Partner to sell to AWS customers.
• AWS India will facilitate issuance of tax compliant invoices to AWS customers in Indian Rupees ('INR') with you as Seller of Record (SoR), as per information provided on the tax registration tab in AWS Marketplace Management Portal.
• AWS Marketplace customer invoices will include Goods and Services Tax (GST), as applicable, on all service charges.
• AWS India will collect the service charges from AWS Marketplace customers as per the generated tax compliant invoice. AWS India will remit the collected GST to you, and it is your responsibility to remit it to the tax authority.
• Disbursements from transactions with AWS customer accounts based in India will be made in INR to your registered bank account located in India.
• AWS India will do Tax Deduction at Source [referred to as Withholding Tax (WHT)] and GST- Tax Collected at Source (GST-TCS) before making your disbursements. AWS India will remit the WHT and GST-TCS to the tax authorities.
• AWS India will charge listing fee(s) with applicable GST and provide you with a tax compliant invoice.
If you are a Channel Partner organized or incorporated in India and transact with AWS customer accounts based in India, you will receive a tax invoice for the transaction between you and your Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) who are organized or incorporated in India.
If you are a seller organized or incorporated outside of India, please note the following:
• You can continue to sell in AWS Marketplace as-is. Invoices will continue to be issued from AWS Inc. in US Dollars (“USD”) to your customers in India.
• GST will not be charged on your listing fee(s).
If you are a Channel Partner organized or incorporated outside of India, you can continue to sell in AWS Marketplace without making any changes. Invoices will continue to be issued from AWS Inc. in US Dollars (“USD”) to your customers in India.

The Service Terms for AWS Marketplace Sellers (“Seller Terms”) (https://aws.amazon.com/legal/seller-terms/) will be updated to reflect this change, and your continued use of AWS Marketplace after the change will constitute your acceptance of the updated Seller Terms.

Required actions before launch:

• Actively communicate this change to your organization’s functional partners including, but not limited to, product, marketing, sales, accounting, tax, treasury, and accounts payable.
• Initiate the process of onboarding as a registered Seller on AWS Marketplace to sell your offerings to AWS customers. For more details on seller onboarding requirements, tax obligations, disbursement preferences, etc., please visit our FAQ page at (https://aws.amazon.com/legal/awsin/).

If you have additional questions after reviewing the FAQs, please contact your AWS account representative or create a case with AWS Marketplace Seller Operations team (https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/contact-us/).

Sincerely,
Amazon Web Services

Now Available: Multiple Group Assignment for CloudConnexa

Managing access for cross-functional users just got easier. With Multiple Group Assignment, you can assign each user to one Primary User Group and up to 20 Secondary User Groups for additive access to resources, ensuring they always have the right access without duplicating configurations or creating user-specific groups. Automate assignments through the API or your Identity Provider for accurate, scalable access control.

DNS Log is Now Out of Beta!

A strong security posture requires more than a first line of defense — you need visibility. DNS Log acts as the “eyes and ears” of your network, showing which domains were accessed, blocked, or unreachable — critical for troubleshooting, compliance, and spotting security gaps.

Now officially out of beta, DNS Log includes key updates that make it more powerful than ever:

Advanced Filters – Zero in on specific domains/IPs, DNS attributes, users, or endpoints to reduce noise and quickly identify threats.
Log Streaming Customization – Choose exactly which DNS Log data to stream to your SIEM by User Group, Network, or Host for targeted monitoring.

With these enhancements, DNS Log delivers sharper insights, faster threat detection, and greater confidence in your security.

name: [Action Required] AWS Lambda end of support for Python 3.9 [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-EAST-2]
description:
Sat, 16 Aug 2025 06:19:08 +0000
[Action Required] AWS Lambda end of support for Python 3.9 [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-EAST-2]
devops@grexit.com
Hello,

[AWS Health may periodically trigger reminder notifications about this communication if resources remain unresolved.]

We are contacting you as we have identified that your AWS Account currently has one or more AWS Lambda functions using the Python 3.9 runtime.

We are ending support for Python 3.9 in Lambda on December 15, 2025. This follows Python 3.9 End-Of-Life (EOL) reached on October 30, 2025 [1]. End of support does not impact function execution. Your functions will continue to run. However, they will be running on an unsupported runtime which is no longer maintained or patched by the AWS Lambda team.

As described in the Lambda runtime support policy [2], end of support for language runtimes in Lambda happens in several stages.

Starting on December 15, 2025, Lambda will no longer apply security patches and other updates to the Python 3.9 runtime used by Lambda functions, and functions using Python 3.9 will no longer be eligible for technical support. Also, Python 3.9 will no longer be available in the AWS Console, although you can still create and update functions using Python 3.9 via AWS CloudFormation, the AWS CLI, AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM), or other tools.
Starting January 15, 2026, you will no longer be able to create new Lambda functions using the Python 3.9 runtime.
Starting February 15, 2026, you will no longer be able to update existing functions using the Python 3.9 runtime.

We recommend that you upgrade your existing Python 3.9 functions to the latest available Python runtime in Lambda before December 15, 2025.

Your impacted Lambda functions using the Python 3.9 runtime are listed on the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

This notification is generated for functions using the Python 3.9 runtime for the $LATEST function version. The following command shows how to use the AWS CLI [3] to list all functions in a specific region that is using Python 3.9, including published function versions. To find all such functions in your account, repeat the following command for each region:

aws lambda list-functions --region us-east-1 --output text --query "Functions[?Runtime=='python3.9'].FunctionArn"

Starting 180 days before deprecation, you can also use Trusted Advisor to identify functions using the Python 3.9 runtime [4].

If you have any concerns or require further assistance, please contact AWS Support [5].

[1] https://devguide.python.org/versions/
[2] https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/runtime-support-policy.html
[3] https://aws.amazon.com/cli/
[4] https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/security-checks.html#aws-lambda-functions-deprecated-runtimes
[5] https://aws.amazon.com/support

Sincerely,
Amazon Web Services
