FATHOM

Meeting Purpose

August Aspirations meeting to review progress, KPIs, and recognize achievements across engineering and product teams.

Key Takeaways

R&D has significantly improved speed and agility over the past year, with shorter project cycles and more flexible roadmaps
Several new AI features launched successfully, including auto-tagging and sentiment analysis, with rapid customer adoption
HOT (Hiver for Outlook) business is growing, reaching $276K+ ARR with 8 new paid accounts added last month
Engineering teams have improved efficiency and reduced costs while maintaining high uptime and performance

Topics

R&D Progress and Agility

Shifted to shorter project cycles (< 3-4 months) and more flexible roadmaps
Able to ship more features and respond faster to market feedback
Some trade-offs made (e.g. less exhaustive specifications) but overall benefits outweigh drawbacks
Focus on continually identifying and eliminating time drains to further improve speed

Product Updates and Adoption

Custom Object feature: 10 UGs adopted (6 in July, 4 in August), used in automations
Individual to Shared Inbox Automation: 10 UGs created rules, similar adoption to Custom Object
Freemium performance: 790 new customers onboarded (625 active), 32 conversions to paid (2200 MRR)
Top 25 Charter: 19 GA-specific features shipped, $150K MRR value, 20+ features in pipeline

HOT (Hiver for Outlook) Progress

Reached $276K+ ARR, added 8 new paid accounts ($1000 MRR)
Net MRR increase of $4.4K, reaching $22.4K total
New UI fully launched with 95% user retention
Split layout feature launched and becoming default for new accounts

AI Charter Achievements

Auto-tagging feature: 78 customers activated, 36 completed learning, 95.2% precision rate
Sentiment analysis: 96 customers activated in 2 weeks, 93K+ sentiments analyzed, 99.99% precision
First AI add-on sale completed

Engineering Metrics and Improvements

100% uptime maintained consistently
Reduced alerts and DevOps requests
Slight increase in dev costs due to spot instance issues, being addressed
HOT performance metrics stable or improving across various APIs

Support and Quality Improvements

Best month for reduced number of bugs escalated to L2/L3
Escalation issue density below 2% for first time in 12 months
Some increase in ad-hoc cases, focus area for improvement

Team Size and Efficiency

Sync Engine team reduced from 7-8 developers to 2.5-3 while improving all metrics
DevOps introduced AI assistant (Gini) to reduce friction and improve deployment speed

Next Steps

Continue focus on increasing speed and agility across R&D
Launch more AI features, including AI automations and linking conversations
Improve trial conversion metrics for HOT
Address increase in ad-hoc support cases
Further optimize development costs and infrastructure efficiency
Continue adoption of AI tools across teams to improve productivity

### 5. 🤖 **AI Assistant** (10:15:36 AM)
## 🔍 Environment Analysis: KB Kafka Consumer Restarts

**Status:** ⚠️ Issues Detected

**Critical Findings:**
- The kb-backend-kb-kafka-consumer-deployment pod has restarted 65 times
- Root cause is connectivity failure to the Datadog agent for trace collection
- Pod is functional but continuously attempts to send traces to a non-existent local agent

**Root Cause:** The pod is configured with SEND_METRICS_TO_DATADOG="true" but is trying to connect to a Datadog agent at localhost:8126 which doesn't exist in the pod or as a sidecar container.

**Immediate Actions:**
```bash
# Check the logs to confirm the issue
kubectl logs kb-backend-kb-kafka-consumer-deployment-865f76ddd4-jd4hk -n qa-admirals-4

# Patch the deployment to disable Datadog metrics temporarily
kubectl patch deployment kb-backend-kb-kafka-consumer-deployment -n qa-admirals-4 --type=json \
  -p='[{"op": "add", "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-", "value": {"name": "SEND_METRICS_TO_DATADOG", "value": "false"}}]'

# Restart the pod to apply changes
kubectl rollout restart deployment kb-backend-kb-kafka-consumer-deployment -n qa-admirals-4
```

**Fix Commands:**
```bash
# Create a ConfigMap with proper Datadog configuration
kubectl create configmap kb-kafka-datadog-config -n qa-admirals-4 --from-literal=DD_AGENT_HOST=datadog-agent.qa-admirals-4.svc.cluster.local --from-literal=SEND_METRICS_TO_DATADOG=true

# Update deployment to use the ConfigMap
kubectl patch deployment kb-backend-kb-kafka-consumer-deployment -n qa-admirals-4 --type=json \
  -p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env", "value": [{"name": "APP_NAME", "value": "hiver-ai-kafka-consumer"}, {"name": "SERVICE_TYPE", "value": "kafka-consumer"}, {"name": "DD_AGENT_HOST", "valueFrom": {"configMapKeyRef": {"name": "kb-kafka-datadog-config", "key": "DD_AGENT_HOST"}}}, {"name": "SEND_METRICS_TO_DATADOG", "valueFrom": {"configMapKeyRef": {"name": "kb-kafka-datadog-config", "key": "SEND_METRICS_TO_DATADOG"}}}]}]'
```

**Verification:**
```bash
# Check if pod has stopped restarting
kubectl get pods -n qa-admirals-4 | grep kb-kafka-consumer

# Verify logs no longer show trace failures
kubectl logs -l app=kb-backend-kb-kafka-consumer -n qa-admirals-4 --tail=50

# Monitor restart count
kubectl get pod kb-backend-kb-kafka-consumer-deployment-865f76ddd4-jd4hk -n qa-admirals-4 -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}'
```

The pod is continuously restarting because it's trying to send traces to a Datadog agent that doesn't exist. The error "failed to send, dropping 3 traces to intake at http://localhost:8126/v0.5/traces after 3 retries" indicates the pod is configured to send metrics to Datadog but can't connect to the agent. This is causing the pod to crash and restart. The fix is to either properly configure the Datadog agent endpoint or disable the metrics collection.

What changed?
In order to make EventBridge integration with AWS Health even more highly available, we are introducing back-up regions for events. Previously, EventBridge rules received only Health events affecting the region where the rule is setup. From October 31, 2025 going forward, US-WEST-2 will be the backup region for all other regions in the standard partition, while US-EAST-1 will be the backup for US-WEST-2.

By configuring a backup region, all Health events, both public and account specific, will be sent simultaneously to both the impacted region and to a backup region. We are doing this to ensure that all Health events are still received, even if your primary region is affected by an ongoing issue.

Instructions:
Maintaining the behavior as it is today requires adding a filter on detail.eventRegion. For example, to ensure US-WEST-2 rule only captures events affecting US-WEST-2, add the filter for detail.eventRegion = US-WEST-2.

Hello,

You are receiving this message because you currently have 1 or more Amazon EKS clusters running Amazon Linux 2 (AL2) based AMIs. Amazon EKS will end support for EKS optimized AL2 AMIs on November 26, 2025.

To avoid any disruptions, please migrate your workloads to alternative AMI types before November 26, 2025. While you can continue using EKS AL2 AMIs, EKS will no longer release any new Kubernetes versions or updates to AL2 AMIs after this EOS date, including minor releases, patches, and bug fixes.

A list of your affected resource(s) can be found in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

We recommend upgrading to Amazon Linux 2023 (AL2023) or Bottlerocket AMIs. AL2023 enables a secure-by-default approach with preconfigured security policies, SELinux in permissive mode, IMDSv2-only mode enabled by default, optimized boot times, and improved package management for enhanced security and performance, well-suited for infrastructure requiring significant customizations like direct OS-level access or extensive node changes. Bottlerocket enables enhanced security, faster boot times, and a smaller attack surface for improved efficiency with its purpose-built, container-optimized design, well-suited for container-native approaches with minimal node customizations. Additionally, you can build custom EKS AL2-optimized and AL2-accelerated AMIs [1] until the EOS date (November 26, 2025), or build a custom AMI with an Amazon Linux 2 base instance until the Amazon Linux 2 EOS date (June 30, 2026).

For more information, please visit AL2023 FAQs [2], Bottlerocket FAQs [3], or refer to Amazon Linux 2 to Amazon Linux 2023 [4] or Bottlerocket AMIs [5] documentation for detailed migration guidance.

If you have questions or any challenges taking action by November 26, 2025, please see EKS AL2 & AL2-Accelerated AMIs EOS FAQs [6] or contact AWS Support [7].

All clusters in extended support are backed by technical support from AWS.

If you do not want to use extended support, we recommend that you update your 1.31 clusters to Kubernetes version 1.32 or newer before November 26, 2025. You can also opt-out of extended support by managing your Kubernetes version policy [1]. name: [Action Required] Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL is deprecating minor versions on October 31, 2025 [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]
description:
Thu, 24 Jul 2025 17:18:48 +0000
[Action Required] Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL is deprecating minor versions on October 31, 2025 [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]
devops@grexit.com
Hello,

You are receiving this message because you have one or more instances running Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL minor versions 13.15, 13.16, 14.12, 14.13, 15.7, 15.8, 16.3, or 16.4 that require your attention. The mentioned Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL minor versions will reach end of standard support on October 31, 2025. To learn more about the RDS policies related to major and minor version support, refer to Database Engine Versions section in RDS FAQs [1].

Starting October 1, 2025, you will not be able to create new instances with RDS for PostgreSQL minor versions 13.15, 13.16, 14.12, 14.13, 15.7, 15.8, 16.3, or 16.4 from either the AWS Console or the CLI. RDS will upgrade your databases running versions listed above to PostgreSQL 13.18, 14.15, 15.10, 16.6, or higher during a scheduled maintenance window after October 31, 2025.

We recommend that you take action and upgrade [2] your Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases running minor versions 13.15, 13.16, 14.12, 14.13, 15.7, 15.8, 16.3, or 16.4 to versions 13.18, 14.15, 15.10, 16.6, or higher before October 31, 2025 [3]. Alternatively, you can enable Automatic Minor Version Upgrade [4] to allow Amazon RDS to upgrade your instances.

This is a mandatory engine version upgrade and it requires downtime. To minimize the downtime during the upgrade, you can now use the fully managed Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments that uses physical replication for minor version upgrades [5].

We recommend upgrading these instances to newer minor versions to benefit from patches for known security vulnerabilities, as well as bug fixes, performance improvements, and new functionalities added by the PostgreSQL community. To learn more about documented vulnerabilities of PostgreSQL versions, visit the PostgreSQL security page [6].

Your Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instances running minor versions mentioned above are listed in 'Affected Resources' tab of the AWS Health Dashboard.

If you have any questions or concerns, the AWS Support Team is available on AWS re:Post [7] and via AWS Support Center [8].

[1] https://aws.amazon.com/rds/faqs/#Database_Engine_Versions
[2] https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.PostgreSQL.html
[3] https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/PostgreSQLReleaseNotes/postgresql-release-calendar.html
[4] https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.Upgrading.html#USER_UpgradeDBInstance.Upgrading.AutoMinorVersionUpgrades
[5] https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2024/11/rds-blue-green-deployments-upgrade-rds-postgresql
[6] https://www.postgresql.org/support/security
[7] https://repost.aws
[8] https://aws.amazon.com/support

Sincerely,
Amazon Web Services

name: [Action Required] End of Support Notice for Amazon EKS Optimized Amazon Linux 2 (AL2) AMIs [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]
description:
Sat, 28 Jun 2025 00:10:14 +0000
[Action Required] End of Support Notice for Amazon EKS Optimized Amazon Linux 2 (AL2) AMIs [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]
devops@grexit.com
Hello,

You are receiving this message because you currently have 1 or more Amazon EKS clusters running Amazon Linux 2 (AL2) based AMIs. Amazon EKS will end support for EKS optimized AL2 AMIs on November 26, 2025.

To avoid any disruptions, please migrate your workloads to alternative AMI types before November 26, 2025. While you can continue using EKS AL2 AMIs, EKS will no longer release any new Kubernetes versions or updates to AL2 AMIs after this EOS date, including minor releases, patches, and bug fixes.

A list of your affected resource(s) can be found in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

We recommend upgrading to Amazon Linux 2023 (AL2023) or Bottlerocket AMIs. AL2023 enables a secure-by-default approach with preconfigured security policies, SELinux in permissive mode, IMDSv2-only mode enabled by default, optimized boot times, and improved package management for enhanced security and performance, well-suited for infrastructure requiring significant customizations like direct OS-level access or extensive node changes. Bottlerocket enables enhanced security, faster boot times, and a smaller attack surface for improved efficiency with its purpose-built, container-optimized design, well-suited for container-native approaches with minimal node customizations. Additionally, you can build custom EKS AL2-optimized and AL2-accelerated AMIs [1] until the EOS date (November 26, 2025), or build a custom AMI with an Amazon Linux 2 base instance until the Amazon Linux 2 EOS date (June 30, 2026).

For more information, please visit AL2023 FAQs [2], Bottlerocket FAQs [3], or refer to Amazon Linux 2 to Amazon Linux 2023 [4] or Bottlerocket AMIs [5] documentation for detailed migration guidance.

If you have questions or any challenges taking action by November 26, 2025, please see EKS AL2 & AL2-Accelerated AMIs EOS FAQs [6] or contact AWS Support [7].

[1] https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-ami-build-scripts.html

[3] https://aws.amazon.com/bottlerocket/faqs/

name: [Action Required] Amazon EKS Kubernetes 1.31 end of standard support [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]
description:
Fri, 27 Jun 2025 00:19:59 +0000
[Action Required] Amazon EKS Kubernetes 1.31 end of standard support [AWS Account: 856707897744] [US-WEST-2]
devops@grexit.com
Hello,

[AWS Health may periodically trigger reminder notifications about this communication if resources remain unresolved.]

Standard support for Kubernetes version 1.31 in Amazon EKS will end on November 26, 2025. Starting this date, Amazon EKS clusters running on 1.31 with Kubernetes version policy set to extended will enter extended support. Kubernetes version 1.31 will remain in extended support until November 26, 2026. After November 26, 2026, Kubernetes 1.31 will no longer be supported on Amazon EKS, and all Amazon EKS clusters running on 1.31 will be automatically updated to Kubernetes version 1.32.

You are receiving this message because you currently have 1 or more Amazon EKS clusters running on Kubernetes version 1.31. If you have deleted, or already upgraded your EKS cluster, please disregard this message.

A list of your affected resource(s) can be found in the 'Affected resources' tab of your AWS Health Dashboard.

Amazon EKS clusters in extended support receive ongoing security patches for the Kubernetes control plane. Additionally, Amazon EKS releases critical patches for Amazon VPC CNI, kube-proxy, and CoreDNS add-ons, AWS-published EKS Optimized Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) for Amazon Linux and Bottlerocket, and EKS Fargate nodes for Kubernetes versions in extended support. All clusters in extended support are backed by technical support from AWS.

If you do not want to use extended support, we recommend that you update your 1.31 clusters to Kubernetes version 1.32 or newer before November 26, 2025. You can also opt-out of extended support by managing your Kubernetes version policy [1]. Amazon EKS clusters that are opted-out of extended support will have their control planes automatically upgraded at the end of standard support.

To learn more about the extended support versions pricing, see our announcement [2]. For instructions on how to update your cluster(s), see the Amazon EKS service documentation [3]

To learn more about Kubernetes version support, see the Amazon EKS service documentation [4]

If you have questions or concerns, please contact AWS support [5].

[1] https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/disable-extended-support.html

Before you hit OOO, make sure there's no OOM

As temperatures rise and inboxes fill with “Out of Office” replies, nobody’s got time to worry about Kubernetes autoscaling.

name: Reminder: Complete Know Your Customer Process To Receive Disbursements From AWS Korea
description:
Tue, 13 May 2025 16:06:15 +0000
Reminder: Complete Know Your Customer Process To Receive Disbursements From AWS Korea
devops@grexit.com
[Starting September 15, 2025, emails about AWS Health events will be delivered via the AWS User Notifications service. You can opt-in to this enhanced experience today. See footer for details.]

Hello,

As of April 1, 2025, Amazon Web Services Korea LLC (“AWS Korea”) is the contracting party for South Korea-based buyers who purchase products on AWS Marketplace. Please note that AWS Marketplace sales to AWS customer accounts based in South Korea are facilitated by AWS Korea and that your disbursements from transactions with South Korea-based buyers cannot be disbursed until you complete the Know Your Customer (KYC) and the bank account verification process.

How this affects you:
• Disbursements from transactions with AWS customer accounts based in Korea will be made by a 3rd-party payment processor’s bank account in US Dollars (“USD”) to your registered US bank account, your local Korean bank account which can accept USD disbursements, or virtual US bank account with Hyperwallet. Your disbursements from transactions with South Korea-based buyers cannot be disbursed until you complete the Know Your Customer (KYC) and the bank account verification processes.

Reminder of things you must do:
• Actively communicate this change to all your organization’s functional partners including, but not limited to Finance, Accounts Receivables, Legal, Product, Sales and Tax.
• Review FAQ for getting disbursements (https://aws.amazon.com/legal/awsk/#56-1) to understand the requirements to complete the Know Your Customer (KYC) process, the bank account verification process, and add a secondary user for the KYC procedure.
• Refer to the Seller Guide (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/seller-registration-process.html#completing-the-know-your-customer-process) and Know your customer (KYC) guide (https://external-aws-mp-isvs.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/KYC/KYC_Documents_Guide.pdf) for the step-by-step instructions on completing these steps.

Reminder for Important Communications regarding KYC:
Communications regarding KYC will be sent to your root email address. In order to locate your root email address, navigate to the ‘Settings’ tab in AWS Marketplace Portal, and then go to ‘Notifications’, where your root email address will appear. You will receive communications regarding KYC in your root email address and, if you have any questions, you must respond using your root email address. Please refer to your root email address regularly for KYC communications.

If you have additional questions after reviewing the guide and FAQ, please contact your AWS account representative or create a case with AWS Marketplace Seller Operations team (https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/contact-us/).

Sincerely,
Amazon Web Services

Amazon Web Services, Inc. is a subsidiary of Amazon.com, Inc. Amazon.com is a registered trademark of Amazon.com. This message was produced and distributed by Amazon Web Services, Inc. or its affiliates (https://aws.amazon.com/legal/marketingentities/) 410 Terry Ave. North, Seattle, WA 98109. Copyright 2025, Amazon Web Services, Inc. or its affiliates. All rights reserved. Read our Privacy Notice (https://aws.amazon.com/privacy/).

안녕하세요.

2025년 4월 1일부터 Amazon Web Services Korea LLC('AWS Korea')는 대한민국에 기반을 둔 AWS Marketplace 구매자와의 계약 당사자입니다. 대한민국에 기반을 둔 AWS 고객 계정을 대상으로 한 AWS Marketplace 거래는 AWS Korea에서 처리하며, 대한민국에 주소를 둔 구매자와의 거래로부터 수령한 자금은 고객확인제도(KYC) 절차, 은행 계좌 확인 절차, KYC 절차를 위한 보조 사용자 추가 전에 지급되지 않는 점 확인 부탁드립니다.

영향:
• 대한민국에 주소를 둔 AWS 고객 계정과의 거래 대금은 타사 결제 처리업체의 은행 계좌를 통해 등록된 미국 은행 계좌 또는 USD 지급처리가가능한 한국 은행 계좌 또는 Hyperwallet의 가상 미국 은행 계좌에 미국 달러(‘USD’)로 지급됩니다. 대한민국에 주소를 둔 구매자와의 거래로부터 수령한 자금은 고객확인제도(KYC) 절차, 은행 계좌 확인 절차, KYC 절차를 위한 보조 사용자 추가 전에 지급되지 않습니다.

반드시 해야 할 일:
• 이메일을 수신한 담당자는 제품, 마케팅, 영업, 회계, 세금, 재무 및 자금을 등 조직담당자에게 변경 사항을 적극적으로 안내합니다
• 지급받는 방법 FAQ (https://aws.amazon.com/legal/awsk/#56)를 검토하고, 은행 계좌 확인 절차인 고객확인제도(KYC) 절차를 완료하며, KYC 절차를 위한 보조 사용자를 추가합니다.
• 단계별 지침과 추가 FAQ는 관련 셀러 가이드 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/seller-registration-process.html#completing-the-know-your-customer-process)와 고객확인제도(KYC) 가이드 (https://external-aws-mp-isvs.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/KYC/KYC_Documents_Guide.pdf)를 참조하세요.

KYC 관련 중요 커뮤니케이션 안내:
KYC 관련 연락은 고객의 루트 이메일 주소로 발송됩니다. 루트 이메일 주소 확인을 위해서는, AWS Marketplace 포털 내 '설정(settings)' 탭으로 이동한 후 'notifications(알림)' 으로 가서 표시된 이메일 주소를 확인하시면 됩니다. KYC 관련 연락은 루트 이메일 주소로 받게 되며, 질문이 있으신 경우 반드시 루트 이메일 주소를 사용하여 답변하셔야 합니다.  KYC 관련 연락을 위해 이메일 계정을 정기적으로 확인해 주시기를 바랍니다.

FAQ를 검토한 후 추가 질문이 있는 경우 AWS 계정 담당자에게 문의하거나 AWS Marketplace 지원 팀(https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/contact-us/)을 통해 서포트 케이스를 생성하세요.

Important: You can see the list of affected users under the Affected Resources tab in your AWS Health Dashboard [1]. To stop this deletion, users that are listed in the Affected Resources tab need to launch CloudShell [2] in the us-west-2 Region.
